headline: Anthropic hires fewer juniors, holds more meetings
dek: An internal report shows fewer junior staff in technical roles and more time in meetings.

s2.label: What happened
s2.title: Fewer juniors in technical roles
body: According to an internal Anthropic report cited by TechCrunch and TechRadar, juniors fell from 21% to 14% of the technical workforce since 2025.
Junior share of new technical hires dropped from 27% to 9% over the period, per TechCrunch and TechRadar.

s3.label: How it works
s3.title: Gains credited to AI
s3.body: According to TechRadar, the company says AI use raised:

points.t: Queries per data scientist grew 3.1 times (TechRadar).
Deals closed per salesperson rose 1.7 times (TechRadar).

s4.label: Why it matters
s4.title: More meetings, scarce attention
body: Meeting time per employee rose about 20%, according to TechCrunch and TechRadar.
The report says human attention became the bottleneck: Claude produces text people still must read (TechCrunch).

items.t: Sales calls and job interviews stay human, TechRadar says.
Autonomy and judgment weigh more in hiring, per TechRadar.
The report comes from Anthropic itself, using internal data.

caption.hook: Anthropic hired fewer junior staff and spent more time in meetings over the past year.
body: An internal Anthropic report, covered by TechCrunch and TechRadar, shows juniors fell from 21% to 14% of the technical workforce since 2025. Their share of new technical hires dropped from 27% to 9%.

TechRadar cites gains the company credits to AI, such as 5.1 times more commits per engineer. Meeting time rose about 20%, and the report points to human attention as the new bottleneck. The data comes from Anthropic itself and is framed, the company says, as a signal for other firms.
caption.cta: Should AI shrink the entry-level jobs for people just starting out?
